sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The explanation of the Baal HaGeulah in his maamar emphasizes that the redemption is "in peace," meaning without any war at all, and true peace is when there is no possibility for opposition.

translations.translation: And behold, the explanation of the Baal HaGeulah in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"
(printed in his book Shaarei Teshuvah9),
is that the emphasis in the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is
(in addition to the matter of redemption,
also)
on the manner of the redemption,
that the redemption is in peace, without any war at all10.
And he explains there11,
that the true essence of peace is that there is no opponent at all.
And analogous to this was in the days of Shlomo,
that all the nations were nullified to him.
And seemingly the intention is,
that as long as he has opponents,
even if in practice they do not wage war with him
(because his awe and fear fell upon them12
and the like),
this is not the true essence of peace13.
For when opponents exist, there is a possibility and a place for war,
and the true essence of peace is
(not only that in practice war will not occur,
but)
that there is
(also)
no possibility and place for war.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: True peace existed specifically in Shlomo's days because all nations were nullified to him, unlike Dovid's era where opponents remained, so the redemption "in peace" means the opponent is nullified.

translations.translation: And this is that the matter of peace was specifically in the days of Shlomo,
therefore he was called Shlomo because there was peace in his days14,
for all the nations were nullified before Shlomo
(due to the intensity of his greatness),
and when the opponent is nullified
(so that there is no place for him to wage war),
then it is the true essence of peace.
And this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to King Dovid
(when he wanted to build the Holy Temple)
"You shall not build a house for My name, for you are a man of war"15,
even though at that time
(when Dovid wanted to build the Beis HaMikdash)
he was in a state of rest,
and Hashem had given him rest from all his enemies around16,
for Dovid's rest came through his victory in all the wars,
and not that his enemies were nullified17.
And since in his days opponents still remained
(and there is a place for them to wage war),
this is not the true essence of rest and peace.
And this is "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
that the matter of redemption in peace is that the opponent is nullified,
as it was in the days of Shlomo.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The true essence of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is that former enemies become friends, a level above Shlomo's peace, referring to Dovid's soul as it will be in the future.

translations.translation: And he continues in the maamar18,
that the true essence of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is,
that those who were previously enemies and opponents become lovers.
For this matter is superior even to the peace that was in the days of Shlomo19,
for the peace that was in the days of Shlomo is that all were nullified due to the revelation of light
(but they were not transformed into holiness)20,
and the true essence of peace
(that even the opponent is transformed into holiness)
will be in the future to come,
as it is written21
"Then I will turn to the peoples a pure language, to serve Him with one accord."
And what Dovid said "He redeemed my soul in peace"
[even though in his days the opponents were not nullified, and certainly not transformed into holiness,
for this matter did not exist even in the days of Shlomo and will only be in the future],
is explained in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah22,
that this refers to the soul of Dovid as it will be in the future.
